analyst_view.overall: Early view: Udinese are bottom with 5 points, sacked Kosta Runjaic on 2 November after one point from eight games, and lost 2-1 at Venezia in Paolo Zanetti's first game. Frosinone are 6th and in form, with Antonio Raimondo among Serie A's top scorers after the 5-1 win over Lecce; Gabriele Bracaglia is banned. This is refreshed with team news the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, which is already high. Frosinone's direct, wide attacking (five against Lecce) and Udinese's leaky run support goals, but a new coach like Zanetti usually tightens the defence first, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, split evenly. Frosinone use wide attackers a lot, which can push their share up, but Udinese at home under a new coach should also push forward, so I see no clear reason to move off the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean higher: Udinese are in a relegation fight under a new coach and will be chasing points at home, and Frosinone already have a player (Bracaglia) out on a five-yellow ban, which hints at a side that picks up bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 36.4 shots, which is very high for a Serie A game. I lean lower simply because that is far above normal, and Zanetti's first job at Udinese is likely to be making them harder to play through.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. Frosinone have been clinical, with Raimondo on eight league goals by late October, but I trim nothing firm until team news is in, so I stay with the number.
